subject: Private deployment: license boundary, audit windows & runbook delivery
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@medsync.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: license boundary, audit windows & runbook delivery

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the time earlier. Per our discussion, attaching the initial redlines and a draft Order Form to capture the private (VPC/on-prem) deployment footprint and the operator/access boundaries you asked about. Key items we want to confirm with you and legal before we lock the MSA annex:

- License scope: whether MedSync requires an explicit on-prem license grant for the operator components (operators vs. customer-managed runtime).
- Audit windows: proposed quarterly audit windows + a 10 business day notification baseline in the draft.
- Escrow-like trigger: we call it an "Operator Access Safeguard" in the doc — want your input on acceptable trigger events (SLA failure vs. insolvency).
- Runbook delivery: we included a runbook checklist that we typically ship as a locked artifact during onboarding; your security team flagged specific evidence items we should add.

Attachments: MSA_Redlines_v1.pdf, OrderForm_PrivateDeploy_draft.docx, Runbook_Checklist_v0.3.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the procurement/legal contact who will own redline responses (looped here is Tom if appropriate).
2) Marcus (CC) will propose language options for the license boundary and the Safeguard trigger.
3) Neha (security, CC) will send the evidence matrix and propose the audit cadence we recommend.

Happy to hop on a short call if that helps move the redlines.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Claire Holt <claire.holt@medsync.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@medsync.com>, procurement@medsync.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: license boundary, audit windows & runbook delivery

Jordan —

Thanks for sending these over. A few quick clarifying questions from our side:

1) "Operator Access Safeguard" — our legal wants a clearer definition of the precise triggers and the scope of access that can be requested. For example, would Redwood get console access to customer-managed machines, or are you proposing a snapshot handoff with a custodian?
2) Audit cadence — quarterly is fine but we need to align on maximum window (e.g., a 3-day on-site or 10-day remote window) and whether audits can be third-party.
3) Runbook — the checklist looks good; can you add expected delivery SLAs post-signature and a redaction policy for any internal operator notes?

Looping Tom and procurement — Tom, are you the right point to coordinate the MSA annex redlines and the PO timing? Procurement, please confirm any required PO/contract numbering conventions.

Claire Holt
Head of Procurement, MedSync Health
claire.holt@medsync.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@medsync.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: license boundary, audit windows & runbook delivery

Claire / Jordan —

Thanks. A few proposed redline options so we can pick the right posture:

Option A (standard):
- Grant: Redwood grants MedSync a non-exclusive, perpetual license to use the Software for internal operations within the agreed hosting footprint. Operator binaries used by Redwood to support the deployment are licensed to MedSync solely for the installed deployment and may not be redistributed.
- Operator Access Safeguard: Triggered only on insolvency, court order, or material failure of Redwood's Dedicated infrastructure SLA. Remedy limited to delivery of encrypted snapshot(s) and operator runbook; no ongoing remote console access unless expressly consented.

Option B (customer-favorable):
- Grant: Explicitly convey a limited sublicense for on-prem operator binaries for the duration of the support term; includes right to run, maintain, and transfer to an approved custodian.
- Operator Access Safeguard: Expanded triggers to include extended SLA degradation (>= 3 consecutive major incidents in a 30-day period). Includes an option for third-party forensics with mutually agreed scope.

Audit window language (suggested): Remote audits allowed with 10 business days' notice; on-site audits require 15 business days' notice and are capped at 3 days per audit. Third-party auditors are allowed provided they sign Redwood's mutual NDA and scope is limited to compliance-related artifacts listed in the Runbook Checklist.

I've attached a short excerpt (included in the consolidated redlines I will circulate) that maps each option to commercial/leverage implications. Happy to discuss tradeoffs on a call.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@medsync.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: license boundary, audit windows & runbook delivery

Claire —

Adding the security viewpoint and the specific evidence we can deliver if MedSync chooses Option A vs Option B. High-level:

Deliverables we can commit to at signature (Option A):
- Full runbook PDF (redacted operator notes)
- Signed attestation of access controls and key custody model
- Encrypted snapshot export and checksum procedures (transfer only if Safeguard trigger is validated)

Additional deliverables if Option B chosen (customer-favorable):
- Decryption keys escrowed with neutral custodian (we have partner options)
- Onsite evidence package (logs, config exports) for one post-handover audit within 90 days

For audit mechanics: we prefer remote attestations for routine checks and a scoped on-site (technical) audit limited to three working days. We also require the auditor to operate within a narrow runbook and to use only read-only artifacts; no live interventions without an on-site Redwood engineer.

I'll also attach a small CSV with the evidence matrix mapping each item in the runbook checklist to acceptable formats and redaction guidance. If MedSync needs keys escrowed, we can provide a shortlist of neutral custodians and estimated costs/time.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@medsync.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@medsync.com>, procurement@medsync.com
Date: Sat, 29 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: license boundary, audit windows & runbook delivery

Claire / Tom / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Summarizing agreed next steps and deliverables so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Redwood will circulate consolidated redlines for the MSA annex by COB Mon 11/30 (see attached name: MSA_Redlines_consolidated_20251129.pdf). Marcus will highlight Option A vs Option B impact in a margin table.
2) MedSync to confirm which Option (A or B) they prefer for license scope and the Safeguard trigger. If they choose Option B, expect an additional commercial uplift and a brief custodian selection process.
3) Neha will prepare the evidence matrix CSV (attached to follow) and a vendor list for neutral key custody if requested.
4) Procurement: please confirm PO timing and whether we need a specific contract identifier. Tom, can you confirm who's owning the redline packet on your side?

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute redlines walk-through on Tue or Wed next week — Jordan and Marcus will both attend, Neha optionally for the security items.

Appended: consolidated redlines and the runbook checklist link in HubSpot.

Best,
Jordan

Attachments: MSA_Redlines_consolidated_20251129.pdf
